findings.title: Coverage gauge overstates cross-category coverage for overlapping claims
findings.what: coverageGauge sums each category's already-unioned claimedUsd and clamps the sum to totalBill. That is not a set union across categories. If two categories address the same $5 cell in a $30 bill, the function reports $10 claimed and 33.3% coverage instead of $5 and 16.7%; sufficiently large overlap falsely reports 100%.
findings.fix: Carry a window-wide addressed-cell union from the cascade rollup (or compute one from claims and the priced matrix) and use its directly priced value for gauge.claimedUsd; retain per-category unions only for the category breakdown.
findings.acceptance: Add a regression with two different categories addressing the same priced scope/pool and assert that gauge.claimedUsd equals that cell's price once, while both category rows may independently show the cell's price.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 246-250 add category totals without cell identities. The related baseline cascade only unions cells within each category, so its CategoryCoverage values cannot support the cross-category union claimed by this function.

findings.title: Weekly trendline reruns the entire claim cascade without a workload budget
findings.what: Each render derivation runs the cascade once for the full window and then once for every ISO week. Every weekly run receives the complete claims list, causing claim resolution and cascade setup to scale with weeks × claims even though token entries were already partitioned. No performance probe or budget accompanies this new UI surface.
findings.fix: Pre-index applicable claims by week/scope or extend the cascade to produce whole-window and weekly aggregates in one traversal; add a representative benchmark or probe with an explicit latency and allocation budget.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark covering a representative large window demonstrates that weekly derivation does not repeat all-claim resolution per week and remains within a documented latency/memory budget.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read lines 198-217 and the complete test file: the whole-window cascade is followed by a runReclaimCascade call inside the per-week map, while tests assert only functional results and provide no workload probe or budget.
